title: Unvalidated Quantity Primitives
pattern: Using a raw, unbounded signed/unsigned integer (`i32`, `u32`, `usize`) to represent a quantity or count that has strict domain boundaries.
why_bad: It allows representing structurally invalid states (e.g., ordering `-5` items or `0` items) which can bypass logical checks, trigger division-by-zero errors, or cause integer underflow during mathematical operations.
detection: Look for struct fields named `quantity`, `qty`, `count` typed as a raw integer primitive without an associated validation wrapper.
counterexample:
General collection sizes or memory indices bounded by the execution environment:
```rust
let index: usize = items.len();
```
source: *Domain Modeling made Functional* by Scott Wlaschin (p. 83, 108).
